reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 studies equiatomic Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys without Al, E2 shows Al reduces density in a different alloy system but does not address Hf substitution or high-temperature strength retention, and E3 demonstrates lightweight single-phase alloys with Zr but involves a different base composition and no Hf. None of the passages provide evidence that substituting Hf with Al in HfMoTaTiZr maintains a single-phase solid solution or preserves mechanical properties at elevated temperatures.
premises: Partial substitution of Hf by Al reduces density due to Al's lower atomic mass
The modified alloy retains a single-phase solid solution
Retained refractory elements (Mo, Ta, Ti, Zr) maintain severe lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening
Comparable yield strength and ductility are achieved at room temperature and ~1000 °C
